paragraphs.text: A [Liu An basket tea](liu-an:definition) made in 1985 and kept in its basket ever since. The name points elsewhere, but the leaf is from Qimen County in southern Anhui, from the same small-leaf bush that gives Keemun red tea.

Liu An is a [dark tea](dark:definition): the leaf keeps changing slowly after it is made. Liu An is fired over charcoal, then spread on bamboo mats outdoors for one night to take the [night dew](liu-an:making). It is then steamed soft and packed into small baskets lined with [bamboo leaf](liu-an:basket), so the basket is part of the making, not only the wrapping.
At forty-one years, this basket is old for the tea. Liu An is [said to improve with years](liu-an:ageing) in its basket, and the charcoal edge of a young tea settles as it ages.

brewing.text: Use water at or near the boil, rinse the leaf quickly, and keep the steeps short, each a little longer than the last, in a gaiwan or clay pot; doses run from about 3 to 8 grams for 100 ml, for six to ten or more steeps. A small piece of the basket's bamboo leaf is often brewed with it. Aged tea can also be simmered in a larger pot, about 1 gram to 200 to 300 ml, for a few minutes or longer.

notice.text: A redder, browner liquor, the smoke gone, and the cup moving toward medicinal, woody and camphor notes, often with betel nut.
